title: How to Remove Malware | Step-by-Step Guide to Delete, Uninstall & Clean an Infected Device (Complete Guide)
content_md: To remove malware, disconnect from the internet, restart in Safe Mode with Networking, and run a full security scan to delete what it finds. Next, uninstall suspicious apps and browser extensions, clear leftover startup items, and change your passwords from a clean device if the malware keeps coming back; back up your files and reset Windows. New to the topic? Our guide to what malware is explains what you are dealing with, and the steps below work for most Windows computers. Remove vs delete vs uninstall vs clean: what each term means. These four words describe different parts of the same cleanup. Deleting removes a malicious file, uninstalling removes a malicious program through the normal Windows process, and cleaning removes the traces it left behind, such as startup entries and changed settings. Removal is the whole job: all three together, followed by checking that nothing was left to restart the infection. Can you delete malware yourself? Yes, you can delete most common malware yourself with a security scan and the steps in this guide.
